11.0.0.en: Be of good cheer: let your soul be at rest.

11.0.3.en: The first meeting between Holofernes and Judith began, with his officers standing before him in his great tent, and he sitting on his throne. He began his conversation with Judith by reassuring her, so that she would not be disturbed by the splendor of the place, its might, and the might of his soldiers, and he asked her to calm her mind and be of good heart.

11.0.4.en: Holofernes was clearly moved by Judith's beauty and gentleness, for God had given her grace, not only in attractive beauty, but so that whoever sees her feels comfort and reassurance and is at ease with her. For this reason Holofernes was kind and gentle with her.

11.0.5.en: In reassuring Judith, Holofernes tried to give her an impression of himself and to suggest to her that he was peaceable and not inclined to harm, and that he never harmed any peaceful person who was subject to King Nebuchadnezzar. This is completely contrary to the truth, as we learned from the previous chapters, for the nations who submitted to him, he destroyed their cities and burned them and killed many of them. But he tries to win Judith's affection and to depart from his savage nature.

11.1.0.en: I would have raised my spear: I would have lifted my spear, meaning that I had decided to discipline them.

11.1.1.en: In Holofernes' speech about Judith's people, he spoke courteously, declaring that he had not intended to harm them, and that he had been compelled to besiege the city and prepare to fight it with his soldiers and weapons because they were the ones who had committed an unforgivable error, in that they had despised him by not surrendering themselves and their city to him.

11.1.2.en: The power of influence of the meek children of God upon the people of the wicked world turns them to meekness and calms their savage nature. When lambs are sent out in the midst of wolves, as the Lord Christ said to His disciples (Lk 10:3), they can change the nature of the savage wolves into the nature of the gentle lamb, for the lambs are stronger than the wolves, since the power of God is in them.

11.1.3.en: May you not meet the anger of others with greater anger, nor their pride with harsher pride, but by your humility and meekness break every anger and pride, as the Holy Bible says: "A soft answer turneth away wrath" (Prov 15:1).

11.2.0.en: After Holofernes had reassured Judith and declared his love, forbearance and esteem for her, he asked her to explain to him why she had left her city, come to him, and preferred to take refuge with the Assyrians. Although the reason for her coming had reached him through the advance guards of his soldiers, who had seized her as she came down from the mountain, he wanted to verify it himself and, as the one in charge, learn the facts from her in detail.

11.3.s.en: (2) Judith informs Holofernes of her people's distress

11.3.0.en: Judith began her long conversation with Holofernes in humility, declaring that she was his maidservant and slave and asking his permission for him to listen to her. She even drew his heart to her, not by beauty alone, but by wisdom, for she promised him victory and the achievement of his aims if he would listen to her words.

11.3.1.en: The beautiful thing is that she did not leave her faith and creed out of her speech, but declared that this was from the Lord, to the point that at the end of the conversation (v. 21) Holofernes declared his readiness to submit to her great God. So she was like a missionary to him and to his soldiers, that perhaps they might believe. In her wisdom and humility she resembles Abigail in her conversation with David (1 Sam 25).

11.4.0.en: The wayward souls: the souls that are full of evil and rebel and go astray, and do not submit to Holofernes.

11.4.1.en: The wild beasts of the field: all the beasts that live on the earth.

11.4.2.en: Be led by him: submit to him.

11.4.3.en: After Judith had drawn Holofernes with the hope of achieving his aims, she praised him and his lord King Nebuchadnezzar. She wished him life, which is what every great man desires, to remain in his greatness, and she declared his authority over the whole earth, because he had taken many of the cities of the world around him. For her hearers this meant the hope of taking all the kingdoms of the earth. She glorified the power of the king, which appears in Holofernes, and in this way she turned the praise toward Holofernes, and even regarded him as the true power that ought to be praised, for without him the lord Nebuchadnezzar is worth nothing.

11.4.4.en: She also praised the authority of Holofernes and Nebuchadnezzar in subjecting everyone who opposes them, or whose heart tempts him to resist them, and by this all people, and even animals and beasts, submit to them.

11.5.0.en: Judith also commended his intelligence and wisdom in managing such a mighty army and the kingdoms he had taken. Indeed, everyone agrees that Holofernes alone is distinguished by a mighty power which no one rivals with King Nebuchadnezzar, especially after Holofernes took many lands and subdued them. He is capable in his management and in his military strength, which subdues the nations to him. These words are true and not flattery on Judith's part, because he really is intelligent, strong and a shrewd politician.

11.5.1.en: Every person is affected by praise, and a good word gladdens hearts. So if you want to win the heart of any person, however harsh he may be or far from you, offer him a word of praise or encouragement. May you see the virtues of others and praise them for these, so that you encourage them and win them, and at the same time benefit from these virtues, to acquire them and grow in your spiritual life.

11.6.0.en: After she opened her speech with praise, and Holofernes' heart was ready to believe and accept all that she said, she told him that she knew his decisions against Achior, and declared that she knew Achior's conversation with Holofernes, for Achior had related it to the people of Bethulia when he entered their city.

11.7.0.en: At the same time she confirmed what Achior had said, for she did not give up her faith in the crushing power of her God, but affirmed the truth that Achior had explained to them, that the mighty God of Israel is against them when they sin against Him, and consequently it would be easy for Holofernes to triumph over them. Judith confirmed her words with God's rebukes of His people through the mouth of His prophets for their sins, and His threat of destruction against them for their evils.

11.8.0.en: Then she described the state of her people as being in great terror since they heard the news of the army of Holofernes that besieges them, and she attributed this to their wrongdoing against their God. In this she does not lie, for the person who is strong in his faith and perfect in his trust in God is never disturbed. But this does not mean that God will destroy them, for God makes allowance for His children and helps their weak faith.

11.9.0.en: Had overtaken them: had increased upon them.

11.9.1.en: Lack of water: the need for water.

11.9.2.en: She pictured their suffering and distress, their severe hunger, and how thirst had increased upon them and they were near death. This is indeed true, but God is glorified in the weak, and the more the affliction increases, the nearer it comes to its solution.

11.10.0.en: To show the wrong of the people of God, Judith told how their thirst had increased so greatly that they were about to slaughter their cattle to drink their blood, which is contrary to the Law.

11.11.0.en: Likewise the tithes and firstfruits that they consecrate to God, they were about to take because of the severity of thirst and hunger, although they had not yet done any of this. But Judith is trying to give logical grounds for God's anger against them, for they would break the Law and God would abandon them. Yet God is merciful and appreciates the distress of His children, so He is not angry with them, since they are in a state of death and not in contempt for God's holy things, nor with an intention to break the Law.

11.11.1.en: God is just and merciful, and Judith focused on the first attribute, but it does not stand without the second. In this she supported Holofernes, and at the same time she did not lie, but the mercy of God will appear, which helps His people and rescues them by the favor of His grace and not because they deserve it, since they are sinners. If Judith focused on one part of the truth, which is justice, and did not mention mercy, this is not permission for you always to state half-truths, for you may give a meaning opposite to the truth. We stress here that Judith was in very difficult circumstances, awaiting death and trying to defend herself and her people.

11.11.2.en: May you be, along with your justice, merciful in making allowances for others, especially if you are responsible for them, giving them a chance to correct their mistake and encouraging them, as God treats you with His mercy and love.

11.12.s.en: (3) Judith is sent from God to Holofernes

11.12.0.en: Judith continues her speech in humility, describing herself as a slave, and says that she learned and understood all that had happened to the people of God, and God sent her to inform Holofernes of it.

11.12.1.en: This shows the extent of Judith's faith in what God had revealed to her and sent her on this dangerous mission. This revelation may have been by way of a vision or a dream, as appears in many places in the Holy Bible, such as the dreams of Joseph (Gen 37:5) and the visions and dreams of Paul (Acts 16:9; 18:9). By the power of her words she convinced Holofernes, and he believed that her God had sent her to him, so he was reassured and made her many promises, as appears in (vv. 20, 21). Thus the plan of God appears, which Judith carried out by several means, namely:

11.12.5.en: 4- Her convincing Holofernes that her people were in the wrong and deserved divine punishment.

11.12.6.en: 5- Her speaking with confidence that she was sent by God to Holofernes to accompany him in his entry into Bethulia (and indeed she did enter, with his head with her).

11.13.0.en: "Sheep that have no shepherd": an expression known in the Holy Bible meaning the absence of leadership and the weakness of the people, as in (Num 27:17, 1 Kgs 22:17, Mt 9:36). "Not a dog shall bark at you": an expression among the Semites, that is, the ancient tribes that lived in Asia, and it means calm and the absence of opposition and resistance from people, or even from animals such as the dog. Then she informed him of her intention that she would worship God in prayers and keep the Law, until God declares to her the proper time at which she would accompany Holofernes into the midst of Jerusalem.

11.13.1.en: Thus she persuaded Holofernes to let her practice her worship in his camp, because in that was his benefit, while in truth she wanted to pray and lean on the strong arm of God, that He might accomplish His salvation by her hands. Truly the people of Israel were in the wrong, and troubled like sheep that have no shepherd, and indeed no one could stand firm before Holofernes, but his end would be destruction. This is what Judith meant. But if anyone doubts whether Judith's inexact speech falls under the heading of plain lying and deception, let us make allowance for her, since her circumstances were difficult and she was in a state of self-defense, as she and her people faced the danger of death. We repeat that this is not permission for anyone to deceive in speech to the point of lying, except in war and military maneuvers, as Jael deceived Sisera (Judg 4:17-22) and as Joshua sent two spies to Jericho (Josh 2:1-7). Perhaps when Holofernes heard these words from Judith he thought she was a prophetess, or a priestess of her god, who could hear his voice and tell the future and divine guidance. This was known in pagan worship, and they greatly respected prophetesses and priestesses in the temples of the pagan gods.

11.13.2.en: How great it is for a person to hold fast to his spiritual life in the hardest places and the most adverse circumstances, and God will give him wisdom and opportunity to fulfil his acts of worship, and even make others agree with him and not hinder him.

11.14.0.en: From Judith's words appears her deep relationship with God and her fervent prayers, to which she had been accustomed in her solitude for three and a half years. When this affliction swept over her city, God guided her to this means to save her people, so she is sent by Him to accomplish this work, which we believe God revealed to her clearly, although it is not stated openly in this book. But it is understood from this verse and the other verses in this chapter and before it and after it, because it is impossible for a person to know this strange plan to rescue his people. Despite this divine revelation to Judith, her carrying out of God's plan shows:

11.14.1.en: 1- Her strong faith in the word of God.

11.14.2.en: 2- Her indescribable courage in facing the cruelest personality in the world at that time.

11.14.3.en: 3- Her severe asceticism and her holding fast to worship in all its details, of prayers and fasts.

11.14.4.en: 4- Her readiness to die in obedience to God and to rescue her people. She is a type of Christ the Redeemer, for she entered into death, that is, the private chamber of Holofernes, and came out victorious with the head of Holofernes with her, as Christ died and Satan was bound.

11.15.0.en: In conclusion Judith affirmed that God had become angry with His people because of their many sins, and consequently the way is open for Holofernes to fight them and take their city. She did not mention that God in His mercy forgives His people if they return to Him, and consequently Holofernes would become powerless before the power of God that protects them.

11.15.1.en: It is good that your life be a mission from God, to do His will, and that your only aim be the salvation of your soul and of others. So do not be disturbed if people think ill of you and do not understand you, as long as you are fulfilling the will of God with a pure heart.

11.16.s.en: (4) Holofernes' praise and promises to Judith

11.16.0.en: When Holofernes and his soldiers standing around Judith heard these words and all her previous speech, they sensed the wisdom she possessed, which was no less than her enchanting beauty, and they praised the soundness of her mind and the goodness of her appearance, which they had never seen in another woman.

11.16.1.en: It is the grace of God that He pours out upon His children, so that the people of the world glorify them and submit to them, because the true power in a person is the power hidden within him, that is, the power of God who dwells in him, and not the power of outward appearances. This power is what makes everyone submit to him.

11.17.0.en: Then Holofernes spoke and praised the God of Israel, who guided Judith to hand Bethulia over to him, since Holofernes, like any person, thinks of his own interest. He admired the God of Israel because He achieves his interests and also the interest of Judith, who would be saved from destruction along with the rest of the city.

11.18.0.en: Will be spoken of: will be pointed out or her name mentioned.

11.18.1.en: He promised Judith that if she completed her mission and he took the city, he would take the God of Israel as his god, that is, as one of the gods he worships. He also promised her that she would have a special place in the palace of King Nebuchadnezzar and that he would testify for her and magnify what she had done, for the service of the Assyrians.

11.18.2.en: Do you worship God because He achieves your interests and demands? Or because you have been moved by His love and want to worship Him out of love for Him? Beware lest your heart be occupied with the material promises of the world, of wealth and greatness, for all these pass away. What truly matters is your standing before God and your eternal life.

11.18.3.en: Judith and Holofernes alone in his tent
